newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT SURVIVE "HORROR SHOW" WITH OVERTIME WIN OVER BULLETS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT SURVIVE "HORROR SHOW" WITH OVERTIME WIN OVER BULLETS.

text.p: Tim Hardaway scored seven of his career-high 45 points in overtime as the Miami Heat survived "a horror show" with a 108-105 road victory over the Washington Bullets Friday.

Jamal Mashburn had 23 points and Isaac Austin added 20 points and 13 rebounds for the Heat, who blew a 20-point lead after three quarters but recovered to avenge a home loss to the Bullets the night before that knocked Miami out of first place in the Atlantic Division.
Miami coach Pat Riley gave the Bullets credit. "I have never seen a team so ready to win tonight," Riley said. "We could have easily lost this. It was a horror show.
"We survived, and that's about it.:
Rod Strickland and Juwan Howard had 28 points each for the Bullets, but Howard missed the second of two free throws with 1.4 seconds left in regulation that would have won the game.
Hardaway was 13-for-25 from the field and 13-of-14 from the line. His previous career high was 43 points in 1992 against Boston.
"This is a win. That's all that counts, that's all that matters," Hardaway said.
Yes, this is definitely one of my best nights. I was determined not to lose. Whatever it takes, I will do. Just as long as we don't lose."
In Chicago, Michael Jordan scored 38 points and Scottie Pippen added 24 and nine assists as the Bulls became the first team to clinch a playoff spot with a 104-96 triumph over the Indiana Pacers.
The Bulls (53-7) are 30-1 at home and one win off the pace of last season, when they set the NBA single-season record with a 72-10 mark.
Dennis Rodman, who returned from a one-game suspension for hitting Milwaukee's Joe Wolf in the groin on Monday, grabbed 18 rebounds as the Bulls won for the 11th time in 12 games.
Reggie Miller scored 27 points and Rik Smits 22 for the Pacers, who have lost two straight.

At Los Angeles, Hakeem Olajuwon scored 23 points to move into 14th place on the NBA's all-time scoring list and added 12 rebounds, six assists and five blocks as the Houston Rockets routed the Lakers 111-90.
Olajuwon passed former Laker Elgin Baylor and ended the game with 23,170 points, seven behind Adrian Dantley for 13th place.
The injury-hit Lakers have lost three of their last four games.

In Boston, Patrick Ewing scored 23 of his season-high 39 points in the second half and the New York Knicks rallied from a 15-point halftime deficit to defeat the Celtics for the 19th straight time, 113-102.

Larry Johnson added 19 points and eight rebounds and Charles Oakley had 17 and seven for New York, which has won six straight overall and 11 in a row at Boston. The Knicks have not lost to the Celtics since January 10, 1993.

In Atlanta, Steve Smith and Dikembe Mutombo each scored 20 points as the Hawks defeated the Milwaukee Bucks for the sixth straight time, holding them to eight points in the third quarter en route to a 90-80 victory.
In Utah, John Stockton snapped a tie with a three-pointer and added a pair of free throws in the final 72 seconds to lead the Jazz to their fourth straight victory, 95-88 over the Detroit Pistons.
Karl Malone tied a season high with 41 points to lead the Jazz, and Stockton finished with 16 points and nine assists.
Grant Hill scored 29 points for the Pistons, who have dropped two of their last three games.
In Seattle, Hersey Hawkins scored 26 points and Gary Payton added 24 as the SuperSonics routed the New Jersey Nets 109-90 for their 10th win in 12 games.
Seattle remained 1 1/2 games behind Utah for first place in the Western Conference.

At Golden State, Andrew DeClercq scored all of his nine points in the decisive fourth quarter as the Warriors erased a nine-point halftime deficit and broke a three-game losing streak with a 108-101 victory over the Orlando Magic.
DeClercq hit 3-of-5 field goals and tied a career high with 10 rebounds in just 16 minutes off the bench.
Joe Smith scored 23 points and grabbed eight rebounds and Latrell Sprewell had 21 points and 10 assists for the Warriors, who won for just the second time in nine games.
In Phoenix, Jason Kidd scored 11 of his 15 points in the fourth quarter and Kevin Johnson had 21 points as the Suns won their 22nd straight at home against the Sacramento Kings, 104-87.

At Minnesota, Tom Gugliotta scored 22 of his 30 points in the second half and led four players with double-doubles as the Timberwolves rallied for their franchise-record 30th win, 96-83 over the Denver Nuggets.
In Portland, Clifford Robinson scored 15 points and Arvydas Sabonis and Gary Trent each added 13 to lead the Trail Blazers to their fifth straight victory, 80-69 over the punchless Dallas Mavericks.

In Toronto, Vernon Maxwell scored a season-high 34 points and added seven assists, Cory Alexander had 18 points off the bench and Vinny Del Negro added 17 as the San Antonio Spurs snapped a seven-game losing streak, 106-103 over the Raptors.
